options.text: The boom affected only rural areas.
The baby boom lowered school enrollment.
Consumer demand fell during the boom.
More births raised demand for schools and goods.

questions.explanation: The report ties births to school and goods demand. Falling demand and rural-only limits are contradicted.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Analyze housing discrimination data
questions.stem: A workplace report shows nonwhite families excluded from 9 of 10 new suburban subdivisions.

options.text: Only one in ten subdivisions had restrictions.
Nine in ten subdivisions excluded nonwhite families.
All subdivisions welcomed every buyer.
Restrictions targeted only renters.

questions.explanation: Nine of ten subdivisions excluded nonwhite families. Reversed or denied exclusion is contradicted.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate Brown's implementation
questions.stem: A workplace report evaluates whether Brown v. Board ended segregation quickly.

answer.exemplar: Brown declared segregated schools unconstitutional, but implementation faced resistance and delays in many districts.

questions.explanation: The ruling was historic yet implementation lagged. The report frames both the holding and resistance.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Analyze enforcement of the 1964 Act

stimulus.body: The report notes the Act empowered federal agencies to cut funds from discriminatory programs.

questions.stem: A workplace report asks how the 1964 Act was enforced.

options.text: The Act had no enforcement mechanism.
Enforcement relied only on private lawsuits.
Federal agencies could cut funds to discriminatory programs.
Enforcement came only from state governors.

questions.explanation: The report cites federal fund cutoffs. Private-only or no enforcement is contradicted.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate migration's urban effects
questions.stem: A workplace report weighs the Great Migration's labor gains against urban overcrowding.

options.text: Migration had no effect on cities.
Migration only helped cities with no downsides.
Migration reduced northern labor supply.
Migration boosted northern labor while straining city housing.

questions.explanation: The report balances labor gains and housing strain. No downside or no impact is contradicted.

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Synthesize productivity and employment trends
questions.stem: A workplace report weighs rising productivity against falling manufacturing jobs.

options.text: Rising productivity always creates more factory jobs.
Higher productivity can coexist with fewer manufacturing jobs.
Falling jobs mean productivity also fell.
Productivity and jobs are unrelated in manufacturing.

questions.explanation: The report shows productivity rising as jobs fall. Automatic job growth and inverse linkage are contradicted.

questions.learningObjective: Synthesize policy responses to stagflation
questions.stem: A workplace report weighs tight money against job losses during stagflation.

options.text: Stagflation requires no policy response.
Tight money cures both inflation and unemployment.

questions.explanation: The report balances inflation control against unemployment. Cure-all and no-response claims are contradicted.

questions.learningObjective: Synthesize urban fiscal responses
